text:
mira: quick follow-up from the safetensors/weights-format RFC — i ran into a subtle mismatch when loading quantized shards produced by the new serializer. proposing a small "serializer sanity check" stage on first open so we fail fast instead of silently returning garbled weights. thoughts?

jon: can you paste the failure case? is it checksum vs layout mismatch or dtype mismatch?

mira: looks like dtype+shape mismatch combined with an older quant header. loader accepted the shard because the index matched, but matmul produced NaNs later. here's a minimal repro log:
```
ERROR load_shard: shard=ckpt-0003.safetensors dtype=quant8 shape=[4096, 12288] expected_dtype=float16
WARN fallback: treating as float16, but kernel mismatch may occur
RuntimeError: GEMM returned NaN
```

sasha: ugh. that's the failure mode we've tried to avoid. two quick options:
- eager validate on open (cost: extra reads/parse)
- lazy validate at first execution (lower load cost, but delayed failure + harder to correlate)
Which do we want as default?

dmitri: +1 to eager validate for hosted/Dedicated. Users prefer predictable errors early. For Private we could make it configurable via weight_source flags.

mira: my hybrid idea: light-weight header checks (magic + serializer_version + epoch + small hash) on open, then optional deep-verify (full checksum) async in background. if header mismatch -> immediate error; if header ok but deep-verify fails -> mark shard as corrupt and trigger fallback/rollout. keeps open fast but prevents silent corruption.

jon: header fields sound good. what about API boundary? do we extend WeightSource.open() to return a VerifiedInfo struct? currently it returns a Reader and metadata. I don't want to bloat the caller surface.

mira: proposal: minimal change — WeightSource.open() returns metadata map with keys we already have plus two new optional flags as strings: "serializer_version" and "sanity_status" (values: "unknown"|"header_ok"|"deep_ok"|"corrupt"). that keeps it JSON-y and backwards compatible for callers that ignore it.

sasha: can we standardize the header schema so different serializers (quant, float) can advertise compatibility? e.g. `schema_version`, `serializer_id`, `epoch`, `mini_hash`

mira: yep. suggested header: `magic: SAFETY1`, `serializer_id: "redwood.quant-v2"`, `schema_version: "1"`, `epoch: "2026-03-20-1"`, `mini_hash: "sha1:abcd1234"` plus optional `full_checksum_url` for async verify.

jon: sounds fine. we should document that mini_hash is intentionally short (fast to compute) and only protects against gross mismatches. full checksum is authoritative.

ops: ops note: if we start failing shards on open we need a rollout plan to avoid customer outages. please add a toggle + a canary window.

mira: agreed — default behavior: header check enforced for all new checkpoint uploads; old checkpoints without header will be accepted but flagged as "legacy" and get a background deep-verify if they are accessed. ops toggle to block legacy acceptance for enterprise tenants.

dmitri: implementation notes:
- loader: parse header from the first X bytes (no full parse)
- WeightSource: add `sanity_status` string and `serializer_id` string to metadata
- runtime: on open, if `sanity_status==corrupt` -> attempt fallback model variant (float fallback) and emit metric `weights.corrupt.open`
- background verifier: job that retrieves `full_checksum_url` or computes digest and updates status to `deep_ok` or `corrupt`

jon: do we want CI to validate serializer outputs? maybe add a small integration that writes a shard and verifies header+full-checksum roundtrip.

ci-bot: noted. will add `serializer-roundtrip` integration job to eng-ml CI board, runs on serializer repo PRs.

sasha: one more question — how do we surface this to customers? i think the Console needs a per-checkpoint "sanity" badge and an incidents + email if a deep-verify flips to corrupt for a live model.

ops: +1 for console badge. also add governance: auto-create support ticket on corrupt deep-verify for dedicated/private customers.

mira: next steps i'll open a tiny RFC patch with: header schema, WeightSource metadata keys, runtime reactions (metric + fallback), and a rollout plan with ops toggle/canary. owners: mira (author), jon (loader review), sasha (console surface), ops (rollout). if no objections i'll land design doc by EOD and start a PR early next week.

jon: no objections from me. thanks for catching this.

sasha: SGTM

dmitri: SGTM

mira: cool — filing RFC patch now. tagging @team-eng-ml for visibility :eyes:
